title: Probability theory
stage: Graduate study and qualifying exams in mathematics
audience: a graduate student in the first years of a mathematics PhD preparing for qualifying exams, or a graduate preparing to apply for one
purpose: Learn probability on a measure-theoretic foundation: probability spaces and random variables, independence and the Borel–Cantelli lemmas, expectation and modes of convergence, the weak and strong laws of large numbers, characteristic functions and the central limit theorem, conditional expectation, martingales and the optional stopping theorem, martingale convergence, Markov chains, and Brownian motion in outline, with simulation in Python.
primary_reading: Probability: Theory and Examples by Rick Durrett, 5th edition (free PDF)

weeks.1: Probability spaces, random variables and distributions
weeks.3: Expectation, inequalities and modes of convergence
weeks.4: The weak and strong laws of large numbers
weeks.11: Markov chains: recurrence, transience and stationary distributions

blocks.deliverable: Apply the Borel–Cantelli lemmas to supplied sequences of events.
Prove a weak law with Chebyshev's inequality and check its rate by simulation.
Outline the proof of the central limit theorem and check it by simulation.
Week 7 midterm; compute conditional expectations in supplied examples.
Solve a gambler's ruin problem with the optional stopping theorem.
Classify the states of a supplied chain and find its stationary distribution.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Qualifying-exam dossier in probability: write complete solutions to twenty exam-style problems, prove the strong law of large numbers for variables with finite fourth moments and the optional stopping theorem in full, and test five conjectures by plain-Python simulation (with stated seeds and error bars), explaining which were confirmed and which theorem proves each.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
